title: Embracing the future of Artificial Intelligence in the classroom: the relevance of AI literacy, prompt engineering, and critical thinking in modern education
venue: International Journal of Educational Technology in Higher Education
extended_summary:
This paper addresses how Artificial Intelligence, especially generative AI tools such as ChatGPT, is changing education and what skills are needed to use it responsibly. The central question is not whether AI should be adopted, but how students and educators can avoid common problems such as hallucinations, overreliance, misalignment, unfair use, and weak critical evaluation while still benefiting from AI’s capabilities.

The paper is a conceptual discussion grounded in the author’s experience at a Swiss University of Applied Sciences, combined with a narrative literature review. It focuses on higher education, though the author notes that the ideas may also be useful in K-12 contexts. The paper describes the institution’s internal response to AI adoption, including AI-use guidelines that require transparency, documentation, and critical evaluation of AI outputs. It also reviews practical classroom uses of AI such as experiments, case construction, curriculum support, gamification, and immersive technologies.

The main conclusion is that effective AI use in education depends on building an AI culture supported by AI literacy, prompt engineering skills, and critical thinking. The paper argues for workshops, formal courses, updated guidelines, dedicated staff support, and ongoing institutional engagement rather than relying only on policy documents. It frames AI as a sparring partner rather than a tutor or ghostwriter and emphasizes that responsible adoption requires both technical understanding and ethical awareness.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generic generative AI / large language model chatbots used for text and other content generation, instructional support, brainstorming, and conversational interaction.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper discusses generative AI in education broadly, with examples including ChatGPT and other LLMs, focusing on how students and teachers might use them for writing, classroom activities, and prompt engineering. It is a conceptual discussion and narrative review rather than an empirical study of a single product.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual discussion and narrative literature review with a single institutional case description, not a controlled empirical evaluation of an AI tool. No outcome data, effect sizes, or comparative analysis are reported.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper does not report measured impacts on learning, coaching, or feedback outcomes. It offers recommendations and cautions, but no empirical evidence of positive, null, or negative effects.
